Government constituted a Task Force of technical experts from Telecom

Identification i.e. switch database identifies a group consisting of a set 
of Base Trans-receiver Stations (B TSs) physically located in a given 
SDCA. Subscriber from a given SDCA should be subscribed to one and 
only one User Zone Identification i.e. the one associated with the home 
SDCA where subscriber is actually registered. System Identification Code 
(ID) (used in entire network in Circ les), Network ID (used in switch 
database to identify a network or a part of network) and User Zone ID 
can be effectively used to restrict mobility within the SDCA.

Khadi Gramodyog in Chhattisgarh 
 
† 153. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of AGRO AND 
RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether Government propose to promote Khadi Gramodyog in 
the State of Chhattisgarh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the number of people likely to be benefited from these 
industries? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRO A ND RURAL INDUSTRIES (SHRI 
MAHABIR PRASAD): (a) and (b) For the development of Khadi and 
Village Industries in the country, the Government of India is already 
implementing the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) 
through Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) throughout 
the country including the State of Chhattisgarh. Under this scheme, 
margin money assistance is provided at the rate of 25% of the project 
cost for the projects upto Rs. 10.00 lakhs. For projects costing above 
Rs. 10.00 lakhs, and upto Rs. 25.00 lakhs, rate of Margine Money is 
25% of Rs. 10.00 lakhs, plus 10% of the remaining cost of the project. 
For weaker sections viz. SC/ST/Ex-Servicemen Women/Minority/ 
Physical Handicapped/OBC beneficiaries belongs to NE Region, Sikkim, 
Andaman Nicobar and Lakshadweep etc., the margin money grant is 
30% of the project cost upto Rs. 10 lakhs and 10% of the remaining cost 
of the project upto Rs. 25 lakhs. The scheme is being implemented 
through Public Sector Banks, RRBs, Private Sector Scheduled 
Commercial Banks etc. The borrower is required to invest a contribution 
of 10% of the project cost and in the case of weaker sections, it is 5%. 
Further, for the development of Khadi and Village Industries sector in 
the country including Chhattisgarh, the Government is implementing Rebate/ 
Scheme, Interest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate Scheme (ISEC) providing 
subsidized rate of interest on bank loans and Product Development Design 
Intervention and Packaging (PRODIP) scheme for improved designs. 
(c) Under the REGP scheme,  about 1131 projects have been 
financed, generating 31989 job opportunities (upto 31.03.2004) in the 
State of Chhattisgarh, since its inception in the year 2000-01. Under this 
scheme, for the year 2004-05 a target for generating 15025 job 
opportunities in the State of Chhattisgarh has been fixed.

Maiden Flight By Saras 
*154. SHRI R.P. GOENKA: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a 14-seater civilian passenger aircraft 
'Saras' has been indigenously dev eloped and its prototype made a 
successful flight recently at the HAL Airport, Bangalore; 
(b) if so, the distinctive feature of the aircraft; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the prototype aircraft has exceeded 
its intended weight, reducing the payload it can carry and the range; 
(d) if so, the steps being taken to achieve the desired specifications; and 
(e) the details of surveys conducted to project demand for the 
aircraft for domestic needs and the international market and plans drawn 
for its commercial production? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) Yes Sir, the first prototype of 
the indigenously developed SARAS aircraft VT-XSD had its successful 
maiden test flight on 29th May 2004 at HAL airport, Bangalore. 
(b) The distincitve features of the Aircraft are as follows: 
'SARAS' is a multi-role light transport aircraft designed and developed 
by the National Aerospace Laboratories, Bangalore. It is designed to carry 
14 passengers and the first prototype is powered by two turboprop engines 
(pusher) each developing 850 shaft horsepower (SHP). The second proto 
type will be fitted with a higher power  engine of the same family (1200 
SHP), which will also be the case for the production of standard aircraft. 
SARAS is capable of cruising upto a maximum speed of about 550 km./ 
hr and upto an altitude of 30,000 ft. It has a pressurised cabin and provides 
passenger comfort similar to those provided by the regional jet airliners. It 
is capable of operating from short and semi prepared runways and in hot 
and humid climate. It has a wingspan of 14.7 m. and an overall length of 
14.63 m. The various roles considered for SARAS include commuter, 
aerial survey, air ambulance, VIP transport, light cargo transport etc. 
(c) Yes Sir, the prototype did exceed its intended weight. It is very 
common to have prototypes having higher weight than what is eventually 
achieved by refinements in desgin and fabrication in the production stage. 
In the case of SARAS, the maximum take off weight was estimated as

was done and the actual subsystems were selected. Mechanisms are 
put in place so that specified payload and range are not affected by the

(d) The following steps are taken to meet the desired specifications: 
(i) Reduction of the margin available in the basic structure (based 
on analysis and structural testing); 
(ii) Optimization of the struct ure based on design modifications; 
and 
(iii) Fitting with the higher power engine (1200 SHP) in the 2nd 
prototype to meet the safety standards associated with FAR 25 
requirement under single engine failure conditions. 
(e) The last survey was conduc ted by NAL in December 2001, 
based on primary and secondary surveys coupled with a macro-economic

North Eastern region of the country, based on a development model. 
This has predicted a demand for 18 sm all aircraft in this region by the 
year 2005. In addition of the cargo,  ambulance, aerial survey, executive 
aircraft roles and military requirements are taken into account, the 
demand is expected to be 150 aircrafts in the next ten years.

Statement 
Illegal immigration to foreign countries 
During the past few years, a number of Indian Missions/Posts 
abroad have brought to Ministry's no tice several incidents of Indian 
nationals-individually or in groups-making attempts to migrate to countries 
in Western Europe and North America through illegal and fraudulent 
means. Many of these illegal immigran ts are from Punjab. They try to 
migrate illegally mainly for economic reasons and are often assisted by 
unscrupulous agents and touts to whom they pay large sums of money. 
These illegal immigrants are taken to the developed countries in Western 
Europe and North America through Russia and other Eastern European 
countries which are used as transit countries for the purpose of illegal 
immigration. The general modus operandi for such activities is that after 
leaving India they intentionally lose or destroy their travel documents to 
prevent verification of their real identity/nationality status and their 
repatriation back to India. After reaching the country of their destination 
they either apply for political asylum or refugee status on one ground or 
the other or even obtain fake/forged travel documents establishing their 
right of residence in the country destination. They make use of loopholes 
in the local legal system, including by getting married to a local person 
for the purpose of obtaining citizenship, in order to prolong their stay in 
the country of destination with t he ultimate aim of staying there 
permanently. However, many such illegal immi grants are caught and 
put in foreign jails. 
2. Illegal immigration has largely been taking place from the 
developing and least developed countries to the developed countries in 
Western Europe, North America, Australia and New Zealand. However, 
in the post-9/11 scenario European and North American countries which 
were favoured desinations for illegal immigration have made their rules 
more stringent. The result is that not only the number of persons going 
to there countires as illegal i mmigrants has come down but these 
countries have also started repatriating illegal immigrants to their home 
countries. 
3. The illegal immigration from  India continues unabated and 
various countries of the world, particularly Western Europe and North 
America as also transit countries in Eastern Europe, are swamped by 
85 

RAJYA SABHA [15 July, 2004] 
fresh illegal immigrants from India almost on a daily basis. The number 
of agents and touts also seems to be increasing as illegal immigrants try 
to use all means including illegal means, to reach their destinations. 
4. Both the Central and State Governments have been working to 
identify agents and touts involved in illegal immigration and to take all 
necessary measures against them. The Government is also cooperating 
with the foreign countries for the speedy repatriation of India illegal 
immigrants.
